home.title: Find out what is filling your disk
home.sub: Pick a drive or a folder. DiskLens scans it, then you browse it like File Explorer. Nothing is changed or deleted.
phone.locked: Phone found. Unlock it and choose "File transfer" on the USB notification, then press ⟳.
phone.failed: Could not read the phone. Keep it unlocked with "File transfer" on, then scan again.
phone.note: Phone: only files shown in File Explorer are counted (Android itself and app data are hidden). Delete phone files on the phone or in File Explorer.
scan.title: Scanning {name}
scan.readonly: DiskLens only reads. It does not change anything.

ov.unread: {n} folders could not be read (access denied)
ov.linked: {n} hard-linked files were counted once, like Windows stores them

ov.analysisDesc: Find out which files are safe to delete, which need a look, and which to keep.
ov.dupsDesc: Find identical files and keep just one.
ov.oldDesc: Files you have not opened in a long time.

settings.title: Settings
settings.languageHint: Applies right away. The language file for each one lives in src/i18n, so adding one is just adding a file.
settings.privacy: DiskLens works entirely on your computer. Nothing is sent anywhere.
tray.title: Collector
tray.empty: Drag files or folders here, or press +. Collect first, clean up in one go.
tray.locked: Protected: DiskLens will not delete this
tray.restLocked: This is what is left of a folder. Open it to pick items.
confirm.title: Check before you go on
confirm.sub: {n} items · {size}. This is what happens to each one:
confirm.appAsk: This holds an app's data or settings. I understand and want to continue.
confirm.binDesc: Can be restored any time. Space frees up once the Recycle Bin is emptied.
confirm.moveDesc: Copy to another drive, check the copy, then remove the original here.
confirm.permDesc: Gone right away. Cannot be restored.
confirm.sameDrive: ✕ Pick a folder on a different drive
confirm.spaceBad: ✕ Not enough space: needs {need}, only {free} free
confirm.verify: Check the copy: compare every file with the original before the original is removed. Recommended.
confirm.afterVerified: After copying and checking, the original:
confirm.origPerm: Is deleted permanently · the space frees up right away
confirm.origBin: Goes to the Recycle Bin · can be restored, space not freed yet
confirm.permWarn: This cannot be undone. Files skip the Recycle Bin and Windows cannot restore them.
confirm.secure: Secure erase: overwrite 3 times (zeros, ones, random data) before deleting. Slower. On SSDs the drive may keep old copies internally, so this is not a full guarantee.
done.binNote: The space frees up once you empty the Recycle Bin.
err.VERIFY: The copy did not match, so the original was kept
err.HASLINK: Contains links or junctions, so it was not moved
err.NOSPACE: Not enough space on the destination
err.SAMEDRIVE: The destination is on the same drive
err.DESTINSIDE: The destination is inside the folder being moved
err.DESTPROTECTED: The destination is a system folder
risk.safe.desc: caches and leftovers that come back by themselves or are not needed
risk.caution.desc: your own files, app data and installed things: fine to remove if you know you do not need them
risk.danger.desc: Windows and installed programs need these. DiskLens will not delete them.
an.sub: What is safe to delete, what needs a look, what to keep
panel.pickHint.analysis: Click an item to see what it is and what happens if you delete it.
panel.pickHint.dups: Click a copy to see where it is.
panel.pickHint.old: Click a file to see more about it.
dups.title: Find duplicate files
dups.intro: DiskLens looks for files with the same content in this scan. Windows, Program Files, ProgramData, AppData, node_modules and .git are skipped.
dups.skip: Small files are skipped. Pick the smallest size to look at.
dups.phase.quick: Comparing the start and end of files…
dups.counts: {files} files listed · {cand} with a same-size twin · {hashed} read
dups.save: can be saved from {n} groups of identical files
dups.how: Same size, then same start and end, then the full content (SHA-256).
old.sub: Big files that have not changed for a long time
old.intro: Files of 50 MB or more, not changed for at least
r.unknown.what: DiskLens has no rule for this item yet.
r.unknown.del: Find out what it is first. If it is your own file, keep a copy somewhere else.
r.sysvol.what: Windows keeps restore points and indexing data here.
r.sysvol.del: Restore points and backups would break. Windows does not let you delete it anyway.
r.sysvol.tip: To use less space for restore points: Settings → System → About → System protection → Configure.
r.recovery.what: The Windows recovery environment, used to repair or reset the PC.
r.recovery.del: You could no longer repair or reset Windows when something goes wrong.
r.recycle.what: The Recycle Bin: files you deleted earlier.
r.recycle.del: The files inside are gone for good. Look inside first if you are not sure.
r.recycle.tip: Use Empty Recycle Bin below. DiskLens empties it the same way Windows does.
r.pagefile.what: Virtual memory: Windows uses it as extra RAM.
r.pagefile.del: Cannot be deleted while Windows runs. Turning it off can make programs crash.
r.pagefile.tip: Change its size in: System → About → Advanced system settings → Performance → Advanced → Virtual memory.
r.hiberfil.what: Holds the contents of memory for Hibernate and Fast Startup.
r.hiberfil.del: Cannot be deleted directly. If you turn hibernation off, the file disappears and Hibernate and Fast Startup stop working.
r.hiberfil.tip: Run 'powercfg /h off' in an administrator terminal to remove it.
r.winold.what: Your previous Windows installation, kept after an upgrade.
r.winold.del: You can no longer roll back to the previous Windows version.
r.winold.tip: Remove it with Settings → System → Storage → Temporary files → Previous Windows installation.
r.winbt.what: Leftover files from a Windows upgrade or reset.
r.winbt.del: Usually fine once the upgrade finished. An upgrade in progress would fail.
r.winbt.tip: Settings → System → Storage → Temporary files removes these safely.
r.winsxs.what: The Windows component store. It looks huge because most files are hard links shared with System32.
r.winsxs.del: Windows updates and features break, and Windows may not start.
r.winsxs.tip: Shrink it safely with Disk Cleanup → Clean up system files, or 'DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup'.
r.wininstaller.what: Installer copies Windows needs to repair, update or uninstall programs.
r.wininstaller.del: Programs can no longer be updated, repaired or uninstalled.
r.wintemp.what: Temporary files made by Windows and installers.
r.wintemp.del: Nothing breaks. Files in use are skipped.
r.winupdate.del: Fine after updates are installed. Windows downloads again if it still needs them.
r.winupdate.tip: Settings → System → Storage → Temporary files → Windows Update Cleanup does this safely.
r.winlogs.del: Only the history is lost. Files in use are skipped.
r.dumps.what: Crash reports from blue screens or freezes.
r.dumps.del: Nothing breaks. You only lose information for diagnosing old crashes.
r.prefetch.what: Windows remembers which programs you start so they open faster.
r.prefetch.del: Programs start a little slower for a while, then Windows rebuilds it.
r.windows.what: The rest of Windows itself: system files, drivers and settings.
r.windows.del: Windows breaks and may not start.
r.steamgame.del: The game is gone from this disk. You can download it again, and cloud saves usually stay.
r.steamgame.tip: Uninstall it from Steam so Steam knows it is gone.
r.steamcache.what: Steam shader cache and temporary files.
r.steamcache.del: Nothing breaks. Games may stutter for a moment while shaders are rebuilt.
r.program.del: The program stops working and leaves broken traces behind.
r.program.tip: Uninstall it in Settings → Apps → Installed apps.
r.pkgcache.what: Installer cache used to repair or uninstall programs such as Visual Studio or Office.
r.pkgcache.del: Those programs may fail to update, repair or uninstall later.
r.wer.del: Nothing breaks. Only old error reports are lost.
r.programdata.what: Data shared by a program for all users of this PC.
r.programdata.del: The program may lose settings, licenses or downloaded content, or stop working.
r.usertemp.what: Temporary files made by your apps.
r.usertemp.del: Nothing breaks. Apps make new ones when needed, and files in use are skipped.
r.inetcache.what: Windows and Edge caches, including thumbnail caches.
r.inetcache.del: Nothing breaks. Thumbnails and pages load a little slower once while the cache refills.
r.crashdumps.del: Nothing breaks. You only lose data for diagnosing old crashes.
r.wsl.what: A Linux system (WSL) or Docker data, stored as a virtual disk.
r.wsl.del: Everything inside that Linux system or those containers is lost.
r.wsl.tip: Remove it with 'wsl --unregister <name>', or from Docker Desktop.
r.devcache.what: A download cache for developer tools (npm, yarn, pip, Gradle and others).
r.devcache.del: Nothing breaks. Packages are downloaded again the next time they are needed.
r.nuget.del: Projects download their packages again on the next build.
r.appcache.what: A cache an app keeps to load things faster, such as a browser cache.
r.appcache.del: Nothing breaks. The app is a little slower once while the cache refills. Logins and settings stay.
r.storeapp.what: Data of an app from the Microsoft Store.
r.storeapp.del: The app may lose its settings and downloads, or stop working.
r.storeapp.tip: Settings → Apps → the app → Advanced options → Reset clears its data properly.
r.appdata.what: Settings and data of one app on your account.
r.appdata.del: The app may forget your settings and logins or lose saved data. Its cache folders are usually fine to delete.
r.onedrive.del: Deleting here also deletes from OneDrive in the cloud and on your other devices.
r.onedrive.tip: To free space and keep the files in the cloud, right-click → Free up space.
r.nodemodules.what: Packages installed for a JavaScript project.
r.nodemodules.del: The project will not run until you run 'npm install' again.
r.git.what: The history of a Git project.
r.git.del: All commits and branches not pushed elsewhere are lost.
r.personal.del: Gone unless you have a copy elsewhere. From the Recycle Bin you can still restore them.
r.profile.what: Other files in your user profile.
r.profile.del: Mixed content: settings, app data and your files. Open the folder and pick items one by one.
r.dump.what: A crash or memory dump file.
r.dump.del: Nothing breaks. Only useful for diagnosing a crash.
r.tempfile.del: Usually nothing breaks. If a program is using it, it cannot be deleted.
r.logfile.del: Only the history in it is lost.
r.installer.del: Programs you already installed keep working. You only lose the installer.
r.diskimage.del: Gone unless you can download it again. Check it is not your only copy of a backup.
r.vdisk.what: A virtual disk from a virtual machine, WSL or a backup.
r.vdisk.del: Everything inside that virtual disk is lost.
r.archive.del: Its contents are gone too. If it is a backup, make sure you have another copy.
r.video.del: Gone unless you have a copy elsewhere. Big videos are often the fastest way to free space.
r.photo.del: Gone unless you have a copy elsewhere.
r.backupfile.what: A backup or old copy of a file.
r.backupfile.del: Fine if the original is in good shape. Otherwise this might be your only copy.
r.gamedata.del: The game may stop working or need to download its files again.
upd.title: Updates
upd.availableHint: Download it now. It installs when you restart DiskLens.
upd.readyHint: Restart DiskLens to finish. Your settings and history stay.
upd.portableNote: The portable version cannot update itself. Download the new file from the release page and replace the old one.
upd.devNote: Updates are off when DiskLens runs from source.
upd.auto: Check for updates when DiskLens starts
tray.lockedN.one: 1 item skipped: a protected system item.
tray.nestedN: {n} items are already inside a folder in the collector.
tray.nestedN.one: 1 item is already inside a folder in the collector.
confirm.contentsNote: Only what is inside gets cleaned, directly, like Windows Disk Cleanup does. The folder itself stays, and files in use are skipped.
done.inUse: {n} files were in use and were skipped.
done.inUse.one: 1 file was in use and was skipped.
err.CACHEMOVE: Temp and cache folders are cleaned, not moved
ex.type.doc: A document (.{ext}), for example from Word.
ex.type.sheet: A spreadsheet (.{ext}), for example from Excel.
ex.type.slides: A presentation (.{ext}), for example from PowerPoint.
ex.type.text: A plain text file or notes (.{ext}).
ex.type.code: Source code of a program or website (.{ext}).
ex.type.config: A settings file that a program reads (.{ext}).
ex.type.data: A database or data file that a program uses (.{ext}).
ex.type.exe: A program that can be run (.{ext}).
ex.type.lib: A program component (.{ext}) that programs load while they run.
ex.type.driver: A driver or system file (.{ext}) that lets Windows talk to hardware.
ex.type.shortcut: A shortcut that points to another file or website.
ex.type.update: An update or install package (.{ext}) for Windows or a program.
ex.type.torrent: A torrent file that points to a download.
ex.del.program: {app} may stop working or break. To remove it properly, uninstall {app} in Windows Settings → Apps.
ex.del.game: The game may stop working. Steam can repair it with "Verify integrity of game files".
ex.in.appdata: Data that the app {app} keeps for itself: settings, login, cache or offline files.
ex.del.appdata: {app} may lose its settings, login or offline files and has to set them up again. If {app} is already uninstalled, this is a leftover and is fine to delete.
ex.in.storeapp: Data of the Microsoft Store app {app}.
ex.del.storeapp: {app} may lose its settings or offline data. Resetting the app in Windows Settings → Apps is the safe way to clear it.
ex.in.programdata: Data that {app} shares with every user of this PC.
ex.del.programdata: {app} may lose shared settings or licences. If {app} is no longer installed, this is a leftover and is fine to delete.
ex.del.windows: Windows or one of its features may stop working. DiskLens will not delete it.
ex.in.personal: One of your own files, in the folder {app}.
ex.del.personal: It is gone from this PC once the Recycle Bin is emptied. Keep a copy somewhere else first if you still need it.
ex.del.mine: If this is your own file, it is gone once the Recycle Bin is emptied. Keep a copy somewhere else first if you still need it.
ex.del.progfile: A program that uses this file may stop working. Find out which program it belongs to first.
ex.app.folder: The folder of the installed program {app} by {pub}.
ex.app.folderNoPub: The folder of the installed program {app}.
ex.in.installed: Part of the installed program {app} by {pub}.
ex.app.portable: Probably a program or game folder: it holds .exe files but Windows has no record of installing it.
ex.in.portable: Probably part of the program or game in the folder {app} (it holds .exe files but is not installed through Windows).
ex.del.portable: That program or game may stop working. If you no longer use it, its whole folder is fine to delete.
confirm.phoneMoveDesc: Copy to a folder on this PC, check the sizes match, then delete from the phone.
confirm.phonePerm: Delete from the phone for good
confirm.phonePermDesc: Gone right away. A phone has no Recycle Bin.
confirm.phoneNote: A phone has no Recycle Bin. Each item is copied, its size is checked, and only then is it deleted from the phone. If the copy fails, the item stays on the phone.
err.NOBIN: A phone has no Recycle Bin
err.HELPER: The phone did not answer. Is it still plugged in and unlocked?
r.phonetrash.what: The phone's trash: photos and files you already deleted in the Gallery or file manager. The phone keeps them for about 30 days before removing them.
r.phonetrash.del: They are gone for good, and the Gallery can no longer restore them. Nothing you still use is lost.
r.phonetrash.tip: Look in the Gallery trash first if you might want something back.
r.phonethumbs.what: Small preview pictures the phone made so the Gallery opens fast.
r.phonethumbs.del: Nothing is lost. The phone makes them again when you open the Gallery, which can be a bit slower the first time.
r.phonethumbs.tip: They come back over time, so the space saved does not last.
r.phoneappdata.what: Files an app keeps on shared storage: game data, downloaded maps, offline music or videos.
r.phoneappdata.del: The app loses what it stored here. Games may need to download their data again, and offline files may disappear.
r.phoneappdata.tip: Clearing it from Settings > Apps on the phone is safer.
r.phonewa.what: WhatsApp photos, videos, voice notes and documents from your chats.
r.phonewa.del: The media disappears from your chats on this phone. It is only safe if you have a backup or no longer need it.
r.phonewa.tip: WhatsApp's own Storage menu shows big files per chat.
r.phonedl.what: Files you downloaded on the phone from the browser or apps.
r.phonedl.del: The downloads are gone. Check that nothing here is a file you still need.
r.phonedl.tip: Old installers (.apk) and documents you already read are usually safe.
ov.typesDesc: Every video, photo, song, document and archive, each type in its own tab.
types.sub: All files of one kind, biggest first
types.note: Files of 64 KB and up. Windows and program folders are left out. Double-click a photo or video to preview it.
panel.pickHint.types: Click a file to see more about it.
viewer.phoneFail: Could not load this file from the phone. Is it still plugged in?
